findings.issue: Hash-scroll test failure was first misdiagnosed as a ScrollRestoration problem (trace turns 51-52) when the actual bug was that the Section component never rendered the spec-required id
findings.suggestion: On element-not-scrolled failures, check whether the anchor target exists in the DOM before blaming scroll restoration

findings.issue: TypeScript used with loose `any` loader args and no typecheck was ever run (build strips types without checking)
findings.suggestion: Run `tsc --noEmit` once before declaring done, or drop the TS annotations

findings.issue: Careless one-off tool calls: stray bash (t37), malformed write (t39), nonexistent component name PokemonCardCardList (t42), botched server start (t56), pkill killing own shell (t61)

findings.issue: Build attempted while app.css didn't exist yet (trace turn 46), costing one build cycle
findings.suggestion: Write all imported assets before the first build

findings.issue: home.tsx was written with redundant logic and immediately edited twice (trace turns 33-35) before ever being built
findings.suggestion: Compose the filter/pagination logic carefully in the first write rather than write-then-clean

summary: A disciplined, front-loaded session: the agent read the spec, every test, the fixture, the data and the framework docs before writing code, pre-derived expected counts from the data, and needed exactly one fix cycle. It verified beyond the tests with its own browser screenshots compared against the design references and re-ran the full suite after its final edit. The only blemishes are ~8 careless turns (stray/failed tool calls, one pre-CSS build) and a brief misdiagnosis of the hash-scroll failure before landing the root-cause fix.
